about: Confused Monkey is a blurry, low-light clip of a small monkey clutching the top of its head with both hands, eyes wide, as if it has just been told something its brain refuses to process. The camera is close and shaky, which adds to the feeling of a creature caught in a moment of total overload. It works as a reaction to information that makes no sense: a plot twist, a bill, a set of instructions, your own past decisions. Unlike a calm side-eye, this is full panic-confusion, the hands-on-head pose people do when they cannot even begin to respond.
usage:
Use the top box for the setup, usually starting with “me reading” or “me when”, and the bottom box for the thing that broke your brain. The reveal belongs in the bottom line so the eye lands on the punchline right as it reaches the monkey's frozen face.

It lands best for confusion you brought on yourself (old code, old notes, your own handwriting) or for rules that contradict each other. Keep the lines short; the clip is fast and blurry, so the caption has to be read in one glance.
ideas: my own code from last year
my bank statement after the weekend
me hearing the new patch notes
seeing a question we never covered
